correctness.rationale: For every finite parameter poset, unary types are exactly compatible (down-set, up-set) pairs. Distinct incomparable realizations exist iff the opposite cross-intersections are empty. Each mixed type yields the explicit alternating four-vector in the integral radical, because simultaneous opposite intersections would force a strict two-cycle in the named poset. The neutral vector and pure-type differences leave the block [[0,-Q],[-Q^T,0]], where Q is the nonempty ideal–filter intersection matrix. Complementing the filters and subtracting the full-ideal row reduces Q to a signed zeta matrix on nonempty proper ideals, proving det(Q)=±1 for all parameter posets. Unimodularity gives the stated integral congruence, Smith form, primitive radical, field ranks and inertia. Finite direct transitivity/congruence checks covered 90 poset patterns and 45,913 matrix entries; further integer Smith reductions of five sample shapes had no nonunit factors. Finite tests are explicitly not the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: Classical sources establish random-poset homogeneity, the extension property and down-set/up-set unary-type encoding. Three full published mathematical reports on unary type counting, antichain pair-type totals and two-level pair-type totals do not entail the asserted integral congruence for arbitrary finite bases. The separately recorded chain-only hyperbolic congruence is strictly contained as the special case \(j(A)=|A|+1\); its proof does not establish the universal arbitrary-poset statement. The signed zeta-matrix determinant step is prior classical background. The structural mixed-type radical identity and all-base unimodular decomposition are the present contribution under best-knowledge priority.
residual_risks: An older result phrased as a truncated ideal–filter intersection matrix plus mixed-type compatibility could reproduce the statement without mention of the random poset.
The signed zeta block is classical; historical priority is for the full logical all-base decomposition and primitive radical, not zeta inversion.
Published-record search is not an exhaustive mathematical uniqueness or independence certification.

value.rationale: The all-base theorem identifies a canonical primitive integer radical indexed by mixed unary types, a universal hyperbolic splitting, full characteristic-independent rank and free cokernel, and the exact recovery of the number of order ideals from a logically defined matrix. It applies to every finite poset, including nonchains with branching and disconnected comparability graphs, and is not a renaming of a scalar type count or a single numerical example. The structural decomposition is a natural incidence-algebra bridge likely useful for compatibility, orbit and finite-field-rank questions. It does not purport to settle unrelated counting complexity or eigenvalue spectra.
